observation_summary: The compiler failed to correctly resolve qualified names (e.g., 'ns.foo') when they were declared within a local scope but intended to be global, leading to incorrect type inference and scope management.
reasoning_summary: The fix introduces a new conditional logic block in 'TypedScopeCreator' to determine the correct scope for variable declaration. It checks if a qualified name is rooted in the global scope and, if so, attempts to declare it in the global scope rather than the current local scope. This is a correction to the procedural logic used to resolve and assign scopes to qualified names, fitting the definition of an Algorithm/Method defect.
evidence_used: The fix adds a conditional check: 'if (n.getType() == Token.GETPROP && !scope.isGlobal() && isQnameRootedInGlobalScope(n))'
The fix modifies the scope resolution logic by reassigning 'scopeToDeclareIn' to 'scope.getGlobalScope()' when the condition is met.
The failing tests 'testQualifiedNameInference5' and 'testGlobalQualifiedNameInLocalScope' indicate that the compiler was failing to correctly associate qualified names with the global scope.

alternative_types.why_not_primary: While the fix ensures consistency between local and global scopes, the root cause is the procedural logic (the algorithm) used to determine where a variable should be declared, rather than a broken association between two existing, independent structures.
Although the fix adds an 'if' condition, the purpose of the condition is not to validate input or guard against errors, but to implement a new logic path for scope resolution.
